shortDefinition: Connecting AI responses to verified, real-world information sources to reduce hallucination.
fullDefinition: Grounding refers to the practice of anchoring AI outputs to verified external information. A grounded response is one where claims are linked to specific source documents, database records, or real-world data — making it auditable and verifiable. RAG is a grounding technique. Search-augmented AI (like Perplexity) is another form of grounding.
examples: Perplexity grounds every answer with citations to source web pages
Microsoft Copilot grounds responses in your actual organizational data
